drug_class: Biologic / TNF Blocker (Tumor Necrosis Factor Inhibitor)
purpose: Infliximab-Abda is used to treat certain conditions where your immune system is overactive and causing inflammation, including Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and plaque psoriasis. It helps reduce pain, swelling, and other symptoms caused by these conditions. It is a biosimilar, meaning it works just like the original brand-name drug Remicade.
how_it_works: Your immune system makes a protein called TNF-alpha, and in some diseases, your body makes too much of it, which causes harmful inflammation. Infliximab-Abda attaches to that protein and blocks it, like putting a cap on it so it can't cause damage. By lowering inflammation, it helps your symptoms improve and can prevent further damage to your joints, gut, or skin.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections like colds, headache, stomach pain, nausea, infusion reactions during or after the IV drip (such as flushing, itching, or chills), rash, and feeling tired are among the most commonly reported side effects.
warnings: This medication can lower your immune system's ability to fight infections, including serious ones like tuberculosis (TB) and fungal infections — contact your doctor right away if you develop fever, chills, or persistent cough. There is a small increased risk of certain cancers, including lymphoma. Do not take this medication if you have a serious active infection or moderate to severe heart failure. Tell your doctor about all vaccines you need, as live vaccines should be avoided while on this medication.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an IV infusion (a drip through a needle in your vein) at a clinic or hospital — you cannot take it at home as a pill. The dose and how often you receive it depends on your condition, but a common schedule is an infusion at week 0, week 2, and week 6, then every 8 weeks after that. Your doctor will determine the exact dose based on your weight and condition.
